text:
sara-chen: quick pickup from today's all-hands runtime bit. two asks: 1) what's the exact canary plan for kernel v5? 2) what immediate ops knobs help with the kv-cache eviction spikes that hit low-latency pools? collect short answers here and i'll publish a two-paragraph customer note.

jason-roberts: kernel-v5: finishing last perf jobs now. plan if green: micro-canary (one small pool) in us-west tomorrow AM, expand to cross-region micro-canary 48h later. gates: eviction_rate stable, p99 within 10%, no memory regressions. will post canary id once scheduled.

deploy-bot: Canary planned: kernel-v5 | canary-id=kv5-1755 | region=us-west-2 | status=planned.

anita-garcia: short-term ops mitigations (no code): increase pool reserve_fraction to 0.33 and enable prefix_fold for short windows to reduce KV churn. these are reversible and drop eviction spikes in our staging runs.

trevor-moss: batching tip: enable dynamic_microbatch:true and start with target_batch_size=28 for affected low-latency pools. it reduces p99 tails without lifting p50 much. we'll prototype an auto-tuner next sprint.

maya-singh: i've pushed a small dashboard with the eviction/seq_len overlay: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/runtime/eviction-quickview. ping me for access.

jason-roberts: allocator fix: v5 includes a conservative alloc-predictor fallback that prefers smaller initial KV allocations when seq_len variance is high. rollback: flip predictor flag to legacy mode. PR and runbook incoming.

sara-chen: thanks folks  please drop PR/runbook links here by EOD so i can assemble the customer message. i'll schedule a 20m follow-up tomorrow to look at canary telemetry. :calendar:
